items.name: MA3 NPU
items.note: Two different devices answer to this name and the research could not settle which this record is. MA NPU (grandMA2 era): 485 x 332 x 126 mm, 9 kg, 150 VA, powerCON. grandMA3 processing unit L: 482 x 372 x 87 mm (2U), 5 kg, 200 VA, powerCON TRUE1. No depth or weight asserted until the unit is identified, so the fit and payload checks stay quiet for it rather than using the wrong number. PARTLY RESOLVED 2026-09-11: MA's current line is the grandMA3 processing unit M / L / XL (all 372 mm deep); the grandMA2-era MA NPU is 332 mm. Both are now separate records — ma3_pu_m/l/xl and ma_npu_gma2. Retire this record once the unit on the truck is identified. items.name: GigaCore 10 (discontinued)
items.note: RESOLVED 2026-09-11: GigaCore 10 and 10t are different products, not a rename. The 10 is discontinued; the 10t is current and its datasheet documents exactly this 4-front + 4-rear etherCON + 2-fiber layout, so this record is the 10t. Both share the 220 x 330 x 44 mm chassis; the 10 is 2.8 kg and the 10t 3.6 kg. Kept as its own record because rental stock still carries the 10 — see gigacore10t for the current unit.

items.name: Obsidian NETRON EN12
items.note: A NODE, not a switch — 12 DMX ports off the network, and only 2 network ports. Obsidian's actual switch is the NS8. Depth CONFLICT: Obsidian say 146 mm / 5.7 in and 1.82 kg; Thomann list 161 mm and 1.5 kg, which looks like the EN12i's figures (165.8 mm) — Obsidian's own number is used here. Note Obsidian label the 19in axis 'Length' on the EN12 page and 'Width' on the EN12i page, the same wrong-axis trap that mis-set the Pathport Octo.

name: Rack equipment
note: RU heights, widths, depths and full port maps. ruHeight is a multiple of 0.5. rackWidth is full | half | third. fullDepth false means the device leaves the other face of its U free. depthIn is checked against the case's rackable depth, which in touring is the constraint that actually bites. Devices without depthIn or weightLb were not reached by the 2026-09-11 research pass and are deliberately left unasserted — an absent figure runs no check, a wrong figure fails a load-in.
